root_cause.hypothesis: App-level connection/transaction leak in warden's proving-ground worker (or health-check/poll loop): repeated identical `SELECT count(*) FROM warden_proving_ground` opened in a transaction that never commits/rollbacks, leaving idle-in-transaction connections stuck ~390s. Pattern (same query, ~10 pids, uniform idle duration, near-simultaneous) points to a batch/cron job or connection-pool misuse, not organic traffic. No recent deploy, so likely pre-existing bug surfaced by load/scheduling, not a regression.
evidence: 10 distinct pids all idle-in-transaction on identical query, durations clustered 387-391s (near-simultaneous origin)
long_running_queries=0: query itself finishes fast, transaction just not closed after
locks_waiting=0: no lock contention, purely idle-transaction accumulation
connections_used_pct only 25%: not yet exhausting pool, early-stage of leak
RECENT DEPLOYS empty: rules out new code push as trigger
ruled_out: Slow/expensive query causing timeout (query is simple count, long_running_queries=0)
Connection pool exhaustion as root cause (only 25% used, this is a symptom-in-progress not a cause)

proposal.reasoning: 10 conns stuck idle-in-transaction ~390s, same query, never commit/rollback. App-level tx leak. Conn usage low (25%), no locks waiting yet, but leak grows over time. Killing stuck conns frees them; leak itself needs code fix separately.
proposal.expected_effect: Stuck idle-in-transaction conns terminated, connection slots freed, no active work lost (no long-running queries).
